clue.text: Discovering it's no good moaning?

indicators.note: 'it's no good' says the letter for good is absent from the word for moaning

parts.note: grumbling is moaning or complaining

explanation.surface: Someone decides that complaining gets them nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' takes G out of GRUMBLING. To rumble a plot or a person is to find them out.
explanation.definitionFit: To rumble someone is informal British for to see through or detect them.

clue.text: Match official needs to exercise? Rubbish!

parts.note: a ref is a referee, the official in a football match
to exercise a right is to use it

explanation.surface: A fan scoffs at the idea that a referee needs a workout.
explanation.definitionFit: Refuse is household waste, a synonym for rubbish.

clue.text: US uncle going up to bed could be lucky!

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Uncle Sam personifies the United States
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: An American relative heading upstairs to sleep might get lucky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going up' works because this is a down entry; the definition is loose, as a mascot is something that could bring luck.
explanation.definitionFit: A mascot is a charm or figure kept because it is thought to bring good fortune.

clue.text: In French town skirts sheets, pillowcases, etc

indicators.note: to skirt something is to go round its edge, so the town wraps around the other piece

parts.note: Lens is a town in northern France
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shop in a French town sells bedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skirts' is the container signal, not clothing; 'sheets' likewise is bedding rather than paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Bed linen is the collective term for sheets, pillowcases and similar household textiles.

clue.text: RA unit must destroy plant

indicators.note: to destroy the words is to break them apart and rebuild their letters in another order

explanation.surface: An artillery unit of the Royal Artillery is ordered to wreck a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroy' rearranges the ten letters of RA UNIT MUST; 'plant' looks like an industrial site but is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The nasturtium is a garden flower with round leaves and orange blooms.

clue.text: Ways sailor enters launches

indicators.note: the sailor enters, or goes inside, the abbreviation for ways

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way, so STS are streets
a tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman finds his way into boats being launched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enters' is the container signal; 'Ways' as the plural of a street abbreviation is a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Starts as a noun means beginnings or launches of projects.

clue.text: Ring in, not stopping as unqualified

indicators.note: the ring letter goes in the other word

parts.note: a through train runs without stopping
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Someone phones in without pausing, lacking credentials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal. 'unqualified' looks like lacking credentials but means utter, as in a thorough nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: Thorough can mean complete or absolute, the same as unqualified praise or an unqualified success.

clue.text: Argued with a boy in a water plant

indicators.note: the article and boy sit in the plant word

parts.note: a reed grows in shallow water
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: Someone argued with a lad wading in among the bulrushes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; the second 'a' belongs with the plant, not the boy.
explanation.definitionFit: A reasoned case is one argued out logically.

clue.text: Something worn by strippers starting to strip?

indicators.note: the start of the word strippers gives its opening letter

parts.note: to undress is to strip

explanation.surface: A question about what exotic dancers wear before taking it off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starting' takes S from 'strippers'; UNDRESS follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A sundress is a light, sleeveless summer frock, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Stronghold on nippy headland

parts.note: nippy means quick or fast
a ness is a promontory, as in Loch Ness's neighbour names like Sheerness

explanation.surface: A fort stands on a cold, windswept point.
explanation.definitionFit: A fastness is a secure fortified place.

clue.text: Party chief lands

parts.note: a do is a party
main means chief or principal

explanation.surface: The head of a party touches down, or owns estates.
explanation.definitionFit: A domain is a territory or estate under someone's control.

clue.text: A little sloop fun to sail

indicators.note: letters that sail are tossed about like a boat on waves, giving a new order

explanation.surface: A small yacht is a joy to take out on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to sail' rearranges SLOOP FUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoonful is a small amount of something.

clue.text: Regard as over in time

indicators.note: the word for over sits in the word for time

parts.note: an hour is a unit of time
on can mean over or about, as in a talk on art

explanation.surface: Something is considered finished in good time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; 'Regard' is a verb here, to hold in esteem.
explanation.definitionFit: To honour someone is to hold them in high esteem.

clue.text: Ill-treated person passed student coming in

parts.note: man can mean a person

indicators.note: the student letter comes into the word for passed

parts.note: to hand something is to pass it
L is for learner, a student driver

explanation.surface: A student is shoved and passed along roughly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming in' is the container signal; L for learner comes from the L-plates on British learner drivers' cars.
explanation.definitionFit: To be manhandled is to be treated roughly by force.

clue.text: They've killed about fifty foreigners

indicators.note: the word for foreigners goes about, or around, the numeral

parts.note: strangers are outsiders or foreigners
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Some outsiders have killed around fifty people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts STRANGERS around L.
explanation.definitionFit: Stranglers are people who have killed by throttling.

clue.text: Taught top men on paper to take a cut, perhaps

indicators.note: the editors take in, or hold, the other piece

parts.note: editors run a newspaper; ED is short for editor, and there are two

indicators.note: perhaps says the letters given might be in another order

explanation.surface: Senior newspaper staff schooled to accept a pay cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges A CUT to UCAT, and 'to take' puts it between the two EDs.
explanation.definitionFit: Educated means schooled or instructed.

clue.text: So upset when cream comes before building material!

indicators.note: the first pieces come before the last one in the answer

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as I left
the cream of something is the best of it

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, read from the bottom

explanation.surface: Someone is upset that cream comes before the bricks and mortar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' is a reversal signal because this is a down entry; 'comes before' orders the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Asbestos is a fibrous mineral once used widely in construction for insulation.

clue.text: Where a woolly rubs less

indicators.note: woolly means muddled or vague, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A sheep scratches itself less in a certain place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woolly' rearranges RUBS LESS. 'a woolly' reads as a sheep, but 'woolly' is the anagram signal and 'Where' is the definition, asking for a place.
explanation.definitionFit: Brussels is a place, answering a question about location.

clue.text: Perturbed by quantity drunk, sit trembling inside

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the word for a quantity drunk

parts.note: a draught is a single swallow of drink

indicators.note: trembling letters shake into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone upset by how much they drank sits shaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trembling' is the anagram signal and 'inside' the container signal; 'drunk' is past participle, not tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Distraught means deeply agitated or upset.

clue.text: Films nice new master

indicators.note: new shows the letters made afresh in a different order

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A pleasant new head teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges NICE as CINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinema means films collectively, as an art form.

clue.text: Fight over sweetheart from scratch

indicators.note: in a down clue over means placed above the other piece

parts.note: a scrap is a fight
the heart of sweet is its middle letter

explanation.surface: A row about a lover starts from nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' gives E, the centre of SWEET.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrape is a scratch or graze.

clue.text: Dislike offer to go topless

indicators.note: losing the top removes the first letter of the word

parts.note: to present something is to offer it

explanation.surface: Someone dislikes being asked to strip off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go topless' drops P from PRESENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To resent is to feel bitter or aggrieved about something.

clue.text: Fold when about to go in chest

indicators.note: the word for about goes in the word for chest

parts.note: a chest is a case or box
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Clothes are folded when packed into a trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go in' is the container signal; 'when' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A crease is a line made by folding.

clue.text: Unmarried men ring and go round

indicators.note: M stands for married, so unmarried means without that letter

parts.note: taken as written
a circle is a ring

explanation.surface: Bachelors form a ring and move around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unmarried' removes M (married) from MEN to leave EN.
explanation.definitionFit: To encircle is to surround or circle all the way round.

clue.text: Stagger Queen after little drink last night

indicators.note: the queen's letters come after the other pieces

parts.note: a tot is a small measure of spirits

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of the word night

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone is unsteady after a nightcap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last' takes T from 'night'.
explanation.definitionFit: To totter is to walk unsteadily.

clue.text: Make unfriendly stranger tea for a change!

parts.note: an alien is a stranger or foreigner

indicators.note: change here signals rearranging the letters of tea

explanation.surface: A newcomer offers tea as a peace gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a change' rearranges TEA as ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate someone is to make them hostile or estranged.

clue.text: Some man taking sides is told to stop

indicators.note: some says only part of the run of words is needed

explanation.surface: A man taking sides is ordered to back off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' signals letters hidden across 'sides is told'.
explanation.definitionFit: To desist is to cease or refrain.

clue.text: Jade can't move next door

indicators.note: the letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman named Jade is unable to relocate to her neighbour's house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'move' rearranges JADE CANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjacent means lying next to something.
